title: Sermo I opening: today's joy, David's oracle, and Gabriel's hail

edition.locus: Opera omnia, Greek and Latin (Paris, 1622), Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 10, cols. A-D (PDF p. 34)

source_text: Hodie perennis virtutis texuntur coronae. Hodie sacra benevolorum, et religiosorum, diesque festos studiose colentium capita coronare volens Deus, firmae fidei amatores tanquam vocatos et heredes appellat; supernumque regnum cum studio eos qui caelestia sapiunt, ut se divino incorporeorum chororum ministerio coniungant, vocat. Hodie Davidicum adimpletum est oraculum, quod dicit: Laetentur caeli, et exultet terra. Gaudebunt campi, et omnia ligna sylvae, a conspectu Domini quoniam venit. Et David quidem, ligna dicit: Praecursor vero Domini, arbores facientes fructus dignos paenitentia, immo Domini adventu, nuncupat. At Dominus noster Iesus Christus, perenne gaudium cunctis in ipsum credentibus adnunciat. Ait enim: Videbo vos, et gaudebitis: et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis. Hodie celebre atque ineffabile Christianorum, qui suam in Christum spem sponte obsignarunt, mysterium plane nobis adnunciatur. Hodie Gabriel, qui Deo assistit, ad castissimam Virginem veniens, illud, Ave gratia plena, ipsi adnunciat. Ipsa vero secum cogitante qualis esset illa salutatio: Angelus confestim subiunxit, dicens: Dominus tecum. ne timeas Maria: invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum. Ideo concipies in utero, et paries filium: et vocabunt nomen eius Iesum. Hic erit magnus, et filius Altissimi vocabitur. Et dabit ipsi Dominus Deus sedem David patris eius, et regnabit in Domo Iacob in aeternum: et regni eius non erit finis. Dixit autem Maria ad Angelum: Quomodo istud fiet mihi: quoniam virum non cognosco? nunquid amplius virgo permanebo? nunquid virginitatis dignitas in me prodetur et amittetur? Quae, dum velut admirabunda, secum animo sanctissima Virgo versaret; breviter Angelus sermonis summam profert, ac dicit: Spiritus sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi. Ideoque et quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur filius Dei. Nam quod est, hoc et omnino vocabitur. Convenienter igitur sanctam Mariam ex omnibus generationibus solam gratia elegit.
pass_a_gloss: Today (hodie) crowns (coronae) of perennial virtue (perennis virtus) are woven (texuntur). Today God (Deus), wishing (volens) to crown (coronare) the sacred heads (sacra capita) of the benevolent (benevoli) and of the religious (religiosi), and of those zealously (studiose) keeping (colentes) feast days (dies festi), calls (appellat) the lovers (amatores) of firm faith (firma fides) as if called (tanquam vocati) and heirs (heredes); and the supernal kingdom (supernum regnum, subject, as the Greek he ano basileia shows) with zeal (cum studio) calls (vocat) those who savour (sapiunt) heavenly things (caelestia), in order that they join (coniungant) themselves to the divine ministry (ministerium) of the incorporeal choirs (chori). Today the Davidic oracle (oraculum) has been fulfilled (adimpletum est), which says: Let the heavens be glad (laetentur caeli), and let the earth exult (exultet terra). The fields (campi) will rejoice, and all the trees of the wood (ligna sylvae), from the sight (a conspectu) of the Lord, because he comes (venit). And David indeed says trees (ligna): but the Forerunner (Praecursor) of the Lord names (nuncupat) trees (arbores) making fruits (fructus) worthy of penitence (paenitentia), nay rather (immo) of the advent (adventus) of the Lord. But (at) our Lord Jesus Christ announces (adnunciat) perennial joy (gaudium) to all those believing into him. For he says: I shall see you, and you shall rejoice: and your joy no one shall take from you. Today the celebrated (celebre) and unspeakable (ineffabile) mystery (mysterium, subject) of the Christians, who of their own will (sponte) sealed (obsignarunt) their hope (spes) into Christ, is clearly (plane) announced (adnunciatur) to us. Today Gabriel, who stands by God (Deo assistit), coming to the most chaste Virgin, announces to her that (illud) Hail full of grace (Ave gratia plena). She however thinking (cogitante) with herself of what kind (qualis) that greeting (salutatio) might be, the Angel immediately (confestim) added (subiunxit), saying: The Lord with you. Do not fear, Mary: for you found grace (gratia) with God. Therefore (ideo) you shall conceive in the womb, and you shall bear a son: and they shall call his name Jesus. This one shall be great, and shall be called son of the Highest (Altissimus). And the Lord God (Dominus Deus) shall give to him the seat (sedes) of David his father, and he shall reign in the house of Jacob into eternity: and of his kingdom there shall not be an end. But Mary said to the Angel: In what way shall this happen to me: since I do not know a man? Shall I remain (permanebo) a virgin any more (amplius)? Shall the dignity of virginity (virginitatis dignitas) in me be betrayed (prodetur) and lost (amittetur)? Which things, while as though marvelling (admirabunda) the most holy Virgin was turning (versaret) with herself in her mind (animo); briefly (breviter) the Angel brings forth (profert) the sum (summa) of the speech (sermo), and says: The Holy Spirit shall come over (superveniet) into you, and the power (virtus) of the Highest shall overshadow (obumbrabit) you. And therefore also that which shall be born out of you holy (sanctum), shall be called son of God. For what he is, this also altogether (omnino) he shall be called. Suitably (convenienter) therefore grace (gratia, nominative; Greek he charis) chose (elegit) holy Mary alone (solam) out of all the generations (generationes).

lemmas.gloss: set their minds on heavenly things

choices.choice: Regnum can be subject or object. The facing Greek (he ano basileia spoudazei ... tous ouranophronas) makes the kingdom above the subject, so the English reads 'the kingdom above eagerly calls those who set their minds on heavenly things', not 'God calls them into the kingdom'.

choices.issue: Hodie celebre atque ineffabile Christianorum ... mysterium plane nobis adnunciatur
choices.choice: The subject is mysterium: 'the renowned and ineffable mystery of the Christians ... is plainly announced to us'. The earlier lock had 'gaudium' and 'spem posuerunt', which the print does not have.
'sacra' (the print; not 'facta', a long-s misread) agrees with capita: 'the sacred heads of the kind and the devout'.

David's 'ligna sylvae' rendered 'trees of the forest' in the Psalm and 'trees' in the comment on it; the Forerunner's 'arbores facientes fructus dignos paenitentia' rendered 'trees that bear fruit worthy of repentance'. No object is supplied for 'nuncupat': 'speaks of'.

'nunquid amplius virgo permanebo? nunquid virginitatis dignitas in me prodetur et amittetur?' are Gregory's expansion of Luke 1:34, rendered as two questions after the cited verse and not given a Scripture reference.
'summa' = the sum or main point (Greek to kephalaion): 'sets out the sum of his message'.
Grace is the subject of 'elegit' (Greek he charis exelexato): 'grace chose holy Mary alone out of all generations'. This replaces the earlier 'he marks out', which had no subject in the text.

Print margin 'Psal. 95' = Psalm 96:11-13 in English Bibles. Margin 'Matth. 4' at the Forerunner's words; the words are Matthew 3:8-10, cited so. 'qui Deo assistit' cited as Luke 1:19; 'cogitante qualis esset illa salutatio' as Luke 1:29; 'Dominus tecum' as Luke 1:28. 'ex omnibus generationibus' may echo Luke 1:48; uncertain, not cited.

Not adopted: 'al. ante faciem Domini' (for 'a conspectu Domini'), 'al. pie ac sancte obsignarunt' (for 'sponte obsignarunt'), 'al. Ecce concipies' (for 'Ideo concipies'), 'al. vocabis' (for 'vocabunt').

pass_b_english: Today crowns of everlasting virtue are woven. Today God, wishing to crown the sacred heads of the kind and the devout, and of those who keep the feast days with zeal, names the lovers of firm faith as those called and as heirs; and the kingdom above eagerly calls those who set their minds on heavenly things, so that they may join themselves to the divine ministry of the bodiless choirs.

Today the oracle of David is fulfilled, which says: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult. The fields will be glad, and all the trees of the forest, before the Lord, for He comes (Psalm 96:11-13). David, for his part, speaks of trees; but the Forerunner of the Lord speaks of trees that bear fruit worthy of repentance (Matthew 3:8-10), or rather worthy of the Lord's coming. Yet our Lord Jesus Christ announces everlasting joy to all who believe in Him. For He says: I will see you, and you will rejoice; and your joy no one will take from you (John 16:22).

Today the renowned and ineffable mystery of the Christians, who have freely set a seal on their hope in Christ, is plainly announced to us. Today Gabriel, who stands before God (Luke 1:19), coming to the most chaste Virgin, announces to her that saying: Hail, full of grace (Luke 1:28). And as she was considering within herself what sort of greeting that was (Luke 1:29), the Angel at once added, saying: The Lord is with you (Luke 1:28). Do not fear, Mary; for you have found grace with God. Therefore you will conceive in the womb and bear a son, and they will call His name Jesus. He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give Him the throne of David His father, and He will reign in the house of Jacob forever; and of His kingdom there will be no end (Luke 1:30-33).

Then Mary said to the Angel: How will this be done to me, since I do not know a man? (Luke 1:34) Shall I still remain a virgin? Will the dignity of virginity in me be betrayed and lost? While the most holy Virgin, as if in wonder, was turning these things over in her mind, the Angel briefly sets out the sum of his message and says: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. And therefore the holy one who will be born of you will also be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). For what He is, that He will also surely be called. Fittingly, then, grace chose holy Mary alone out of all generations.
notes: 'supernumque regnum ... vocat': the Latin allows the kingdom to be either subject or object; the facing Greek makes the kingdom above the subject, and the English follows it. 'Hodie celebre atque ineffabile Christianorum ... mysterium ... adnunciatur': the subject is the mystery. 'sacra ... capita' = 'the sacred heads'. Mary's two further questions after Luke 1:34 are Gregory's expansion, not Scripture. 'solam gratia elegit': grace is the subject of 'chose' (Greek 'he charis exelexato'). 'summa sermonis' = 'the sum of his message'. 'omnino' rendered 'surely'. The Psalm is 95 in the Latin numbering (print margin 'Psal. 95'), Psalm 96 in English Bibles. The Forerunner's 'trees bearing fruit worthy of repentance' is Matthew 3:8-10 (the print's margin reads 'Matth. 4'). 'qui Deo assistit' recalls Luke 1:19, and 'what sort of greeting that was' Luke 1:29. 'ex omnibus generationibus' may echo Luke 1:48; uncertain, not cited. Margin variants not adopted: 'al. ante faciem Domini', 'al. pie ac sancte obsignarunt', 'al. Ecce concipies', 'al. vocabis'.
